risks: No site admission: the pit pack stays a standalone kiln-local study, and the cut contract has host=null until LY-010/LY-003 decide.
The city renderer cannot cut terrain. Fitting a 0.8-1.04 m deep pit means replacing an atomic ground tile, which depends on LY-100 and the terrain seats (81-90).
Ownership overlap with LY-054 (pit rim, pit floor use, drying board legs). Without an LY-006 ruling, either seat could cover or leave unsupported the same zone.
Node names such as .001 come from the GLB importer. Exclusion and ports should key on the exact names in this baseline; if the kiln is re-exported, the SHA binding breaks and prep must be redone.
Coplanar contacts (bed bottom -0.6, flue base 0, floor bottom -1.04) can z-fight or be misclassified as intrusion. The test plan separates legal coplanar faces from positive penetration (>0.002 m).
Inherited kiln-internal intersections (kiln_bed x fire_hood) could be misattributed to the pit pack. The baseline counts are recorded and must stay unchanged.
All dimensions are C (card text). No ~180 CE Luoyang kiln evidence was found, so nothing may be described as a historical reconstruction.
Only two LODs exist, so the pit pack cannot honestly supply a third tier.
Surface BVH and discrete rays do not prove solid collision, structural safety, thermal behaviour or human passage. All of these are reported as unverified.
